lenses.smells_idioms: All three bodies use the Petri DSL and output APIs without raw properties or persistent jobs. PetriVisual.kt confirms structure-keyed caching and the explicit cache invalidation used in the timing body.
lenses.imports: Each body uses afield.simulation.petri.*; bodies 2 and 3 also use D2Layout. Preserve stars until coordinator deterministic resolution; no import removal proposed.
lenses.whitespace: The four arc endpoints are authored rows kept together; net construction, timing, verdict and HTML output are separated readably.
lenses.comments: Comments explain dense cyclic topology, seeded optimization, optional helper fallback, and why BOTH caches must be cleared. PetriLayoutSolver.RESTARTS is 48.
lenses.glsl: No GLSL; the inline HTML is presentation for measured values, with a dark background and no gradients.
lenses.live_coding: No fragments or declaration/reset pairs. Each box reconstructs a net and replaces its output. Repeated timing intentionally clears shared caches; no frame loop or listener is added.
lenses.helpers: Existing petri, showPetriNet, frame and cache APIs express the example directly. The repeated philosophers definition keeps three boxes independently runnable; no new shared helper warranted.

summary: Five bodies clearly demonstrate qualified rules and frozen fixtures; the proposal example starts an unmanaged waiting thread that should follow the box lifecycle.

lenses.smells_idioms: qualifiedSource registers its tools, closes the previous instance and owns a stop hook (QualifiedSource.kt). Body 3 independently starts kotlin.concurrent.thread, which is outside that lifecycle.
lenses.imports: No explicit imports in any body; qualified APIs are used from the normal box context. No import changes proposed; coordinator analyzer remains authoritative.
lenses.whitespace: Fixture rows are authored input/outcome pairs and should remain grouped. Folded repetitions intentionally make captures self-contained; do not deduplicate across independent runners.
lenses.comments: Frozen marker is functional data and must remain exact. Inline rule/check comments explain the constrained edit boundary; prose gives the approval sequence and partial retain adapter context.
lenses.live_coding: No fragment/reset markers. qualifiedSource reruns preserve histories, but the background thread in body 3 can remain after a rerun closes its replays; follow-up output needs cancellation ownership.
lenses.helpers: Use existing run-owned coroutine/frame facilities for follow-up polling, or the existing build card/agent wait. No new helper proposal; retain adapter is deliberately a partial named argument.

findings.issue: The proposal follow-up waits in a JVM thread with no box stop hook. Re-running qualifiedSource closes the previous source and replay runner, while this thread can still wake and call proposeRebaseline on that stale instance. StudyBuilds.await blocks the caller and does not establish box ownership.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the raw thread with a run-owned asynchronous follow-up that yields while the recorded replay is active and stops with the box; capture the source/job before the asynchronous boundary. Use an IO dispatcher only if retaining blocking await, then return to the normal box/main context for proposal UI.
findings.verification: Replay docs.qualified-sources.proposal; rerun and stop the box during replay and verify no stale proposal/error appears and no waiting thread remains.

verification_needed: Replay docs.qualified-sources.proposal, including stop/rerun while pending; capture the real approval card.

summary: Five asynchronous Loris bodies explain useful operations, but no future or completion callback is owned by a box run; expose the whirlpool controls with units.

lenses.smells_idioms: All five bodies start CompletableFuture work and display progress/results from continuation callbacks. LorisClient async methods use supplyAsync with no Box/run registration; the native request timeout/finally cleanup does not make callbacks current after a rerun.
lenses.imports: Bodies use precise visualizer/loader imports, workspace.path, CompletableFuture, and kotlin.math names. Intro includes several Field and math packages; preserve all until coordinator deterministic analysis. No unsupported star-removal suggestion.
lenses.whitespace: Named chunk start/duration and edit scales are clear. The nested partial/point copies preserve immutable model structure; introduce creative whirlpool values near those existing controls rather than compressing the transformation.
lenses.comments: Box titles give the operation sequence, but the whirlpool coefficients lack units: the 4 term is cycles across the selected interval whereas 12 * chunkDuration is Hz. Add a short explanation at the editing point.
lenses.glsl: No GLSL; all spectral transformations are Kotlin and CPU/native offline work.
lenses.live_coding: No fragments or duplicate reset lines. The futures are not retained or guarded, so old work can publish into a rerun. Do not assume cancelling a dependent CompletableFuture interrupts the native worker; define stale-result suppression separately.
lenses.helpers: Existing transformed, crop, distill, dilate, morph and visualizationHtml APIs are already concise. A shared run-owned future convention could replace repeated stale-result/progress/error handling; proposal below is new, distinct from approved helpers.

findings.issue: The analysis future and its callbacks are detached from the run. All five boxes repeat this shape, and LorisClient uses common-pool supplyAsync without box ownership. Stopping or rerunning a box can leave old analysis/resynthesis callbacks displaying results after the new run.
findings.proposed_change: Own the operation and its progress/result publication in the active run, suppress callbacks from previous runs and cancel work where the API supports real cancellation. If process interruption requires an API addition, retain that as a separate helper change rather than claiming future.cancel stops the worker.
findings.verification: Launch a cold-cache analysis, rerun with changed settings and stop before completion; verify only current results/progress reach the box and inspect native-worker cleanup.

findings.snippet: val octaves = 1.5 * envelope * sin(2 * PI * 4 * u)
findings.issue: Octave excursion, sweep count, shutter rate and bandwidth blend are buried in nested point transforms. In particular 4 is cycles across the chunk and 12 is Hz, so editing them requires decoding different time scalings.
findings.proposed_change: Name the excursion in octaves, sweep cycles, shutter rate in Hz and noise-bandwidth blend beside chunkStart/chunkDuration; add one intent comment about the sin-squared entry/exit envelope. Keep the transform itself explicit.
findings.verification: Compile/replay loris_spectral_whirlpool with the same defaults; compare transformed partials and listen to real resynthesis before and after.

helper_proposals.title: Run-owned future results and progress
helper_proposals.rationale: Five boxes start native futures and independently attach display/error callbacks. A shared ownership convention should prevent stale completion after stop/rerun without pretending CompletableFuture cancellation interrupts a native process.
helper_proposals.before: client.analyzeWavAsync(..., onProgress = { display("status", it) }).thenAccept { display("result", it) }.exceptionally { ... }
helper_proposals.after: A run-owned operation adapter registers a generation, gates progress/completion, returns errors through the box and invokes a supported worker-cancellation hook; final API spelling requires design.
helper_proposals.existing_or_declined_check: Read BOX_CODE_HELPER_IDEAS.md: no approved/declined future adapter. Checked RunScope.kt and ReturnValueRegistry.kt for Future/CompletionStage support and LorisClient async implementation; no run registration found. Existing frames/go can provide ownership but do not automatically interrupt supplyAsync native work.
helper_proposals.verification: Cold-cache concurrent/rerun/stop tests must prove current-only publication and actual native-worker cleanup; preserve bounded request timeout and cached results.

verification_needed: Run all five bodies with the optional Loris worker; verify real source/reconstruction audio and partial visualizations.
Exercise cold-cache stop/rerun ordering and confirm no stale progress/results.

summary: Five bodies provide a real editable GPU study and asynchronous recording; teach normal inherited shader properties and explain the shader interface.

lenses.smells_idioms: Renderer context is correctly captured before frames, and owned=lab deliberately keeps final cleanup bound to that study across reruns. Named lookup closes a prior study only when present. Four getPropertyRaw shader reads bypass existing Box.vertex/fragment properties.
lenses.imports: Includes neural library star and explicit context/control/vector/Path APIs. Coordinator deterministic analyzer must decide redundancy; do not drop the star from inspection alone.
lenses.whitespace: Kotlin and GLSL are densely spaced. Coordinator formatter should expand operators/arguments while preserving the grouped creative controls and shader formulas; semantic review is the missing interface explanation.
lenses.comments: The imagePath comment and hot-reload failure message explain the editing loop. Record loop checks frozen controls and restores time/recording in finally. Add shader coordinate and uniform units at the point of use.
lenses.glsl: Read both stages. Vertex generates an oversized fullscreen triangle and flips UV Y. Fragment uses frame.x as seconds and frame.yz as pixel dimensions, confirmed by OpenDlssNrStudy.render, then emits linear LDR color for NR. There are no SSBOs, manual dispatches or barriers in these bodies.
lenses.live_coding: No authored fragments or declaration/reset pairs. Sliders update captured mutable values. frames finalizers own study closure and recording-state restoration; preserve owner/owned aliases because they pin resources across asynchronous work.
lenses.helpers: Box.vertex and Box.fragment already exist as inherited nullable strings; reuse them. Approved fullscreenTriangle is a Kotlin setup helper, not justification to remove the authored GLSL property. No new helper proposal.

findings.issue: Construction and reload each read vertex/fragment through raw property strings and casts although normal inherited shader properties are already available. This teaches the escape hatch for the main editing path and ignores shader inheritance.
findings.proposed_change: Read the normal vertex and fragment properties for both study construction and reload; resolve their nullable contract explicitly once per operation with a useful missing-shader error. Preserve the captured renderer/study references used by frames cleanup.
findings.verification: Compile/replay the transcript in source-only mode and with the optional NR backend; edit fragment, reload valid and invalid GLSL, and confirm the working pipeline is retained after invalid code.

findings.snippet: layout(push_constant) uniform Study { vec4 frame; } pc;
findings.issue: The main editable shader does not document the host-provided frame packing or color space. A reader must inspect OpenDlssNrStudy.render to learn x=time seconds, yz=source pixel dimensions and w=unused; the vertex UV flip and linearize call are similarly unexplained.
findings.proposed_change: Document frame packing beside the uniform, the Y flip/UV convention in vertex, and the final conversion to linear LDR beside output. Keep procedural stroke comments and all bindings unchanged.
findings.verification: Compile both shaders and use a real GPU capture to confirm source, NR and grade panes retain their orientation and brightness.

verification_needed: Compile/replay with real GPU in source-only and NR-ready states; capture the three comparison panes.
